title: Make the install entries work where the repo package is missing
head: 0d0ec3507cbd
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates
decision: Publishable draft with 2 visible findings (ollama-bin removal, menu-test failure) and 4 collapsed findings

leads.summary: The new ollama-bin installation is not removed by Remove > AI > Ollama
leads.consequence: On the AUR fallback, the installed package's literal name is ollama-bin (it provides ollama). The existing Remove entry is offered because pacman -Q ollama resolves provides, but the remover passes only ollama, ollama-cuda, ollama-rocm and ollama-vulkan to omarchy-pkg-drop. That helper selects installed literal package names using pacman -Qq, so it executes no package removal, still stops the service, deletes the models and prints 'Ollama and its models have been removed.' A second attempt repeats the same non-removal; the package and binary remain installed.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F3 (published as visible finding 1)

leads.summary: The existing menu test rejects the five new Install-row when guards
leads.consequence: The pinned head test exits 1: it expects Chromium Account to be the only guarded Install action, while the five new guards add four terminals and LM Studio. The same test passes at the intake quattro tip. The author's reported test/cli pass does not cover test/shell.d/menu-test.sh; update the invariant and the docs/guard contract, while testing genuinely unavailable versus already-installed software.

leads.summary: A missing or invalid sync database hides even installed terminal and LM Studio rows
leads.consequence: pacman -Si checks validity of all configured sync databases before package lookup and exits nonzero when any are invalid. The helper turns every error into false and discards stderr. After the menu guard batch finishes, when:false hides the row before disabled: can dim or mark an already installed package. Stock Foot is present in install/omarchy-base.packages; during a fresh offline-to-online pacman-config transition or invalid sync database, even Foot disappears from Install > Terminal until databases recover, without indicating why. An installed foreign package absent from sync repositories stays hidden until a repo offers it again.
leads.triage: source-only; Opus run shows a partially missing db still answers from other dbs, contradicting part of the lead; the all-missing case is subsumed by the published installed-row finding and its suggested guard; dropped as separate claim

leads.summary: -Si cannot resolve the provides and group targets that omarchy-pkg-add accepts
leads.consequence: The helper explicitly promises to ask the same target question as omarchy-pkg-add but -Si only tests literal sync package names, whereas -S calls alpm_find_dbs_satisfier, then falls back to groups. For a configured repo that has a provider or a group but no literal package with the supplied target, the guard returns false and hides a valid install action. This also affects optional callers of the public 'omarchy pkg available <packages...>' command, including repository-qualified target constraints. Compare with pacman's own -Sp transaction resolution (without installing anything), or guard only exact-name targets and document that narrower contract.

leads.summary: Unavailable accelerator package causes an AUR CPU install even if repo ollama is available
leads.consequence: If nvidia-smi (or rocminfo) is on PATH but the corresponding ollama-cuda (or ollama-rocm) package is not in the configured sync repos, the installer never checks for the plain ollama package. It immediately asks yay to install ollama-bin, which ships the base binary rather than the separate CUDA components. On a GPU machine with plain repo ollama available this unnecessarily changes install source and GPU variant, while an AUR failure aborts a repo-installable Ollama. The fallback test in reproducers demonstrates the exact selection using package-command stubs.
leads.triage: control flow true but no realistic repo where GPU package is missing while ollama exists (ALARM has neither); dropped

leads.summary: Five x86_64-only repository installer rows are left unguarded
leads.consequence: The class of other repo-only Install actions whose named package's maintained Omarchy recipe declares only x86_64 includes Dropbox (dropbox), Spotify (spotify), Hermes Desktop (hermes-desktop), Minecraft (minecraft-launcher), and Heroic (heroic-games-launcher-bin). These still display as installable on aarch64 although their installers call omarchy-pkg-add, so selecting them goes to a failing package transaction, defeating the stated missing-package boundary. Edge is AUR-backed and is excluded from this set; Zed's Omarchy package has an aarch64 build. The guard policy needs to enumerate the full repo-only list (and multi-package installers such as Dropbox).
leads.triage: overlaps Opus note on other unguarded rows (#8645); scope choice of PR, not published as finding; issue #8645 linked

leads.summary: Open #13362 independently adds a different omarchy-pkg-available and guards Ollama out on ARM
leads.consequence: PR #13362 is diverged rather than stacked and independently creates bin/omarchy-pkg-available with a different implementation (one sync-db scan plus satisfier lookup), changes menu availability throughout, and guards Ollama on omarchy-pkg-available ollama. A three-way merge of the menus at their real common base has conflict markers, and the newly added checker path is an add/add collision. If #13362's Ollama guard is retained, it suppresses the very aarch64 AUR fallback this PR introduces. Coordinate/rebase these two implementations, choose one helper and keep Ollama visible where AUR fallback works.
leads.triage: new lead; coordinator verified via gh api: #13362 adds bin/omarchy-pkg-available (cached pacman -Slq) and when: omarchy-pkg-available ollama; Opus self-check confirmed add/add conflict by merge-tree; published in Details

leads.summary: The GPU hardware correction in #10472 conflicts with the moved Ollama action
leads.consequence: Open diverged PR #10472 changes the old inline menu action from command-presence checks (nvidia-smi/rocminfo) to hardware checks (omarchy-hw-nvidia/omarchy-hw-amd), specifically to stop choosing CUDA on a non-NVIDIA GPU merely because nvidia-smi is installed. This PR moves the old selection unmodified into a new script. Three-way menu merge conflicts at install.ai.ollama; simply choosing this PR's menu line silently drops #10472's correction, leaving the original false GPU selection in the new script. Carry over hardware detection if both changes merge.

leads.summary: Open #11025 and #12932 would remove the new ARM Ollama fallback if their guard wins the menu conflict
leads.consequence: Open diverged #11025 and #12932 independently add the same x86_64-only when guard to both LM Studio and Ollama, replacing the inline Ollama action, while this PR leaves Ollama visible on ARM to use ollama-bin. Neither head is stacked with this PR or the other. Merge-file tests show conflicts at the exact two lines; both other PRs also change the menu-test fixture to expect an x86-only guard. If the architecture guard is kept, aarch64 users cannot reach the fallback; if this PR's lines are kept, their guard fixture is obsolete. Resolve code and tests together.

leads.summary: New availability and Ollama fallback lack tests exercising package results or removal
leads.consequence: The existing guard tests exercise installed-package helpers, not the new sync-availability helper; remove-ai-test checks the Ollama menu row but not removal of the new ollama-bin package. Mutating `omarchy-pkg-available` to always succeed, or `omarchy-install-ai-ollama` to pass a wrong fallback package to omarchy-pkg-aur-add, is not detected by test/cli, bin-style-test, menu-guards-test or remove-ai-test. Add stubbed sync-db and AUR/GPU cases and an exact-package removal assertion alongside the existing helper tests. The unrelated menu-test regression first needs fixing before the full shell suite can pass.
leads.triage: folded into suggested changes (remove-ai-test case); generic test request otherwise omitted

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** Remove > AI > Ollama leaves the fallback's `ollama-bin` installed but deletes the models and reports success.

### Removing Ollama leaves `ollama-bin` installed

`omarchy-pkg-present ollama` matches `ollama-bin` through `provides`, so Remove offers Ollama, but `omarchy-remove-ai-ollama` drops only exact names such as `ollama-cuda`. It still deletes `/var/lib/ollama` and `~/.ollama` and reports success.

**Suggested change:** add `ollama-bin` and its split `-bin` variants to that drop list, with a case in `remove-ai-test.sh`.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 0d0ec35)</summary>

# Reproducer: Remove > AI > Ollama cannot uninstall the `ollama-bin` the new fallback installs

`omarchy-install-ai-ollama` installs AUR `ollama-bin` (which `provides=("ollama")`) when no repo package resolves. The Remove row's guard `omarchy-pkg-present ollama` resolves through that provide, so the row is offered, but `omarchy-remove-ai-ollama` only drops the exact names `ollama ollama-cuda ollama-rocm ollama-vulkan`, and `omarchy-pkg-drop` matches exact `pacman -Qq` names.

The script below uses the real `pacman` against a throwaway local database holding only `ollama-bin`, and a `sudo` stub that only logs, so nothing on the system is touched. Save it as `remove-ollama-bin.sh` and run it from a checkout of the PR head `0d0ec3507cbd10c6585cc6cf363e4661113b1cba` with `ROOT=$PWD bash remove-ollama-bin.sh`.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Remove > AI > Ollama after the AUR fallback installed ollama-bin.
# Uses the real pacman against a throwaway local database (no system access)
# and a sudo stub that only logs. Run from an omarchy checkout: ROOT=$PWD.
set -euo pipefail
ROOT=${ROOT:-$PWD}
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

mkdir -p "$tmp/db/local/ollama-bin-0.35.0-1" "$tmp/db/sync" "$tmp/gnupg" "$tmp/bin" "$tmp/home/.ollama"
echo 9 >"$tmp/db/local/ALPM_DB_VERSION"
printf '%%NAME%%\nollama-bin\n\n%%VERSION%%\n0.35.0-1\n\n%%PROVIDES%%\nollama\n\n' >"$tmp/db/local/ollama-bin-0.35.0-1/desc"
: >"$tmp/db/local/ollama-bin-0.35.0-1/files"
printf '[options]\nDBPath = %s/db/\nGPGDir = %s/gnupg\nSigLevel = Never\n' "$tmp" "$tmp" >"$tmp/pacman.conf"

printf '#!/bin/bash\nexec /usr/bin/pacman --config %s/pacman.conf "$@"\n' "$tmp" >"$tmp/bin/pacman"
printf '#!/bin/bash\necho "sudo $*" >>"%s/sudo.log"\n' "$tmp" >"$tmp/bin/sudo"
chmod +x "$tmp/bin/pacman" "$tmp/bin/sudo"
: >"$tmp/sudo.log"

export PATH="$tmp/bin:$ROOT/bin:$PATH" HOME="$tmp/home"

echo "installed: $(pacman -Qq | tr '\n' ' ')"
if omarchy-pkg-present ollama; then
  echo "Remove > AI > Ollama is offered (when: omarchy-pkg-present ollama succeeds)"
fi
omarchy-remove-ai-ollama
echo "privileged calls:"
sed 's/^/  /' "$tmp/sudo.log"
echo "installed after: $(pacman -Qq | tr '\n' ' ')"
if grep -q -- '-Rns' "$tmp/sudo.log"; then
  echo "PASS: the package was removed"
else
  echo "FAIL: nothing was uninstalled; ollama-bin is still installed"
  exit 1
fi
```

Actual output at the PR head (stdout; exit status 1):

```text
installed: ollama-bin 
Remove > AI > Ollama is offered (when: omarchy-pkg-present ollama succeeds)

Ollama and its models have been removed.
privileged calls:
  sudo systemctl disable --now ollama.service
  sudo rm -rf /var/lib/ollama
installed after: ollama-bin 
FAIL: nothing was uninstalled; ollama-bin is still installed
```

The same output was produced on the PR merged onto `quattro` `8b4eae6` (its `omarchy-pkg-drop` also matches exact names). Deleting `/var/lib/ollama` while `ollama-bin` stays installed also removes a directory that package owns.
</details>

### `test/shell.d/menu-test.sh` now fails

It asserts `install.service.chromium-account` is the only Install row with `when:`, the `docs/menu.md` Guards convention. The five new guards break it, so `./test/shell` fails at this head.

**Suggested change:** update the test and `docs/menu.md` to allow an availability `when:` on Install rows.

<details><summary>More findings</summary>

#### An installed Ghostty or LM Studio can vanish from Install

A false `when:` hides a row before `disabled:` is read. A terminal installed from a package no sync database carries (for example AUR `ghostty-git` on Arch Linux ARM) now disappears instead of reading as installed.

**Suggested change:** guard as `omarchy-pkg-present X || omarchy-pkg-available X`.

**Reproducer (fails at 0d0ec35):**

# Reproducer: an installed terminal disappears from Install when no sync database carries its package

`MenuModel.isVisible` hides a row whenever its `when:` answered false, before `disabled:` is consulted (`shell/plugins/menu/MenuModel.js` lines 255-257 at the head). With the new `when: omarchy-pkg-available ghostty`, a machine where Ghostty is installed from a package no sync database carries loses the row, instead of keeping it dimmed and marked as installed. `ghostty-git` (AUR, `arch=(x86_64 aarch64 i686)`, `provides=ghostty`) on Arch Linux ARM, which has no `ghostty` package, is one such case.

The script uses the real `pacman` against throwaway databases (local: `ghostty-git` providing `ghostty`; sync: only `foot`), the shipped menu's own guard script and `isVisible`. Save it as `installed-row-hidden.sh` and run it from a checkout with `ROOT=$PWD bash installed-row-hidden.sh` (needs `node`).

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Install > Terminal > Ghostty on a machine where Ghostty is installed from a
# package no sync database carries (ghostty-git, which provides ghostty, is
# built for aarch64). Real pacman against throwaway databases; the shipped
# menu's own guard script and visibility logic decide the row.
# Run from an omarchy checkout: ROOT=$PWD (needs node).
set -euo pipefail
ROOT=${ROOT:-$PWD}
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

mkdir -p "$tmp/db/local/ghostty-git-1.3.1-1" "$tmp/db/sync" "$tmp/gnupg" "$tmp/bin" "$tmp/repo/foot-1.0-1"
echo 9 >"$tmp/db/local/ALPM_DB_VERSION"
printf '%%NAME%%\nghostty-git\n\n%%VERSION%%\n1.3.1-1\n\n%%PROVIDES%%\nghostty\n\n' >"$tmp/db/local/ghostty-git-1.3.1-1/desc"
: >"$tmp/db/local/ghostty-git-1.3.1-1/files"
printf '%%FILENAME%%\nfoot-1.0-1-aarch64.pkg.tar.zst\n\n%%NAME%%\nfoot\n\n%%VERSION%%\n1.0-1\n\n%%ARCH%%\naarch64\n\n' >"$tmp/repo/foot-1.0-1/desc"
(cd "$tmp/repo" && tar -czf "$tmp/db/sync/extra.db" *)
printf '[options]\nDBPath = %s/db/\nGPGDir = %s/gnupg\nSigLevel = Never\n[extra]\nServer = file:///nonexistent\n' "$tmp" "$tmp" >"$tmp/pacman.conf"
printf '#!/bin/bash\nexec /usr/bin/pacman --config %s/pacman.conf "$@"\n' "$tmp" >"$tmp/bin/pacman"
chmod +x "$tmp/bin/pacman"
export PATH="$tmp/bin:$ROOT/bin:$PATH"

ROOT="$ROOT" node -e '
  const fs = require("fs"), path = require("path"), { execFileSync } = require("child_process")
  const menu = require(path.join(process.env.ROOT, "shell/plugins/menu/MenuModel.js"))
  const items = menu.parseMenuJsonc(fs.readFileSync(path.join(process.env.ROOT, "default/omarchy/omarchy-menu.jsonc"), "utf8"))
  const row = items.find(item => item.id === "install.terminal.ghostty")
  console.log("when:     " + row.when)
  console.log("disabled: " + row.disabled)
  const out = execFileSync("bash", ["-c", menu.guardScript({ [row.id]: row })], { encoding: "utf8" })
  console.log(out.trim())
  const when = {}, disabled = {}
  for (const line of out.trim().split("\n")) {
    const [id, tag, value] = line.split(":")
    if (tag === "w") when[id] = value === "1"
    if (tag === "d") disabled[id] = value === "1"
  }
  const visible = menu.isVisible({ [row.id]: row }, [row.id], when, row)
  console.log("installed (disabled: succeeded): " + disabled[row.id])
  console.log("row visible: " + visible)
  if (disabled[row.id] && !visible) { console.log("FAIL: an installed terminal vanished from Install instead of reading as installed"); process.exit(1) }
'
```

Actual output at the PR head `0d0ec3507cbd10c6585cc6cf363e4661113b1cba` (exit status 1; identical on the PR merged onto `quattro` `8b4eae6`):

```text
when:     omarchy-pkg-available ghostty
disabled: omarchy-pkg-present ghostty
install.terminal.ghostty:w:0
install.terminal.ghostty:d:1
installed (disabled: succeeded): true
row visible: false
FAIL: an installed terminal vanished from Install instead of reading as installed
```

Actual output at the merge base `692c02c` (exit status 0):

```text
when:     
disabled: omarchy-pkg-present ghostty
install.terminal.ghostty:d:1
installed (disabled: succeeded): true
row visible: true
```

With the row's guard changed to `omarchy-pkg-present ghostty || omarchy-pkg-available ghostty` (same harness, PR head), the guard reports `install.terminal.ghostty:w:1` and the row stays visible and dimmed.


#### Each availability guard adds a `pacman -Si` fork to every menu open

The guard batch runs on every menu load and open. Presence checks are answered in-process from one `pacman -Q` snapshot, but each `omarchy-pkg-available` row forks the helper plus a `pacman -Si` that loads every sync database. On one x86_64 machine the five new guard lines took a median of 751 ms per batch, against 98 ms for the existing presence prelude and 158 ms for one `pacman -Slq`.

**Suggested change:** answer `omarchy-pkg-available` inside the guard helpers from one `pacman -Sl` snapshot, built only when a guard uses it (not implemented or measured here; #13362 has a cached `pacman -Slq` version of this helper).

**Measurement:**

# Measurement: cost of the five `when: omarchy-pkg-available ...` guards in the menu's guard batch

Every `when:` in the menu runs in one bash batch on each (re)load and each open (`Menu.qml` `evaluateGuards`, called from `openExistingMenu`). Presence checks are answered in-process from one `pacman -Q` snapshot (`MenuModel.js` `guardHelpers`); `omarchy-pkg-available` is not, so each of the five new rows forks the helper, which runs a separate `pacman -Si` that loads every sync database.

Measured with the script below (run from a checkout of the PR head `0d0ec3507cbd10c6585cc6cf363e4661113b1cba`; `REVIEW_OUTPUT` is any writable directory; needs `node`, `pacman`, `pacman-conf`, `gawk`; all pacman calls are read-only queries). It extracts the exact guard lines and prelude that `MenuModel.guardScript` generates for the shipped menu and times them 9 times each, alongside single `pacman` calls.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Cost of the PR's `when: omarchy-pkg-available ...` guards, measured with the
# real pacman reading this machine's sync databases (read-only; -Si takes no
# lock). usage: timing.sh <head-source-root> [rounds]
set -u
HEAD="$1"
ROUNDS="${2:-7}"
out="$REVIEW_OUTPUT/timing"
mkdir -p "$out"
ulimit -c 0
export PATH="$HEAD/bin:$PATH"
export OMARCHY_PATH="$HEAD"

pacman-conf --repo-list >"$out/repos.txt" 2>&1 || true
ls -l /var/lib/pacman/sync/ >"$out/syncdir.txt" 2>&1 || true
uname -m >"$out/arch.txt"

# The guard lines MenuModel generates for the head menu's pkg-available rows,
# and the existing prelude (one pacman -Qq/-Qi snapshot) for comparison.
OUT="$out" ROOT="$HEAD" node -e '
  const fs = require("fs"), path = require("path")
  const menu = require(path.join(process.env.ROOT, "shell/plugins/menu/MenuModel.js"))
  const items = menu.parseMenuJsonc(fs.readFileSync(path.join(process.env.ROOT, "default/omarchy/omarchy-menu.jsonc"), "utf8"))
  const sub = {}
  for (const it of items) if (it.when && it.when.includes("omarchy-pkg-available")) sub[it.id] = { id: it.id, when: it.when }
  const script = menu.guardScript(sub)
  const lines = script.split("\n").filter(l => l.startsWith("if { ")).join("\n") + "\n"
  const prelude = script.split("\n").filter(l => !l.startsWith("if { ")).join("\n") + "\n"
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(process.env.OUT, "available-lines.sh"), lines)
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(process.env.OUT, "prelude.sh"), prelude)
' 2>"$out/node.stderr"
echo "node exit: $?" >>"$out/node.stderr"

measure() {
  local name="$1" script="$2" i start end rc
  for ((i = 1; i <= ROUNDS; i++)); do
    start=$(date +%s%N)
    bash -c "$script" >"$out/$name.last.stdout" 2>"$out/$name.last.stderr"
    rc=$?
    end=$(date +%s%N)
    printf '%s\t%d\t%d\t%d\n' "$name" "$i" "$rc" $(( (end - start) / 1000000 )) >>"$out/timings.tsv"
  done
}

: >"$out/timings.tsv"
measure prelude_snapshot "$(<"$out/prelude.sh")"
measure five_pkg_available_guards "$(<"$out/available-lines.sh")"
measure one_pacman_Si_single 'pacman -Si alacritty'
measure one_pacman_Si_five 'pacman -Si alacritty foot ghostty kitty lmstudio-bin'
measure one_pacman_Slq 'pacman -Slq'

# medians (ms)
```

# Reproducer: what `omarchy-pkg-available` answers versus what `omarchy-pkg-add` resolves

`pacman -Si` matches exact package names only (pacman `src/pacman/sync.c`, `sync_info`, a `strcmp` over each sync db's package cache). `pacman -S`, which `omarchy-pkg-add` runs, also resolves virtual provides, groups and version constraints (`process_target` / `process_targname`: `alpm_find_dbs_satisfier`, then the group fallback). For the five names this PR guards the two agree; the helper's comment and summary claim more than that. An option-shaped argument also reads as available because `pacman -Si --help` prints usage and exits 0 (current `quattro` passes `--` in `omarchy-pkg-add`, `-aur-add`, `-present` and `-missing` after "Treat command operands as literal values").

The script uses the real `pacman` against a throwaway sync database (`alacritty`; `gvim` providing `vim`; `ttf-a` in group `fontgroup`) and touches nothing on the system. Save it as `pkg-available-semantics.sh` and run it from a checkout of the PR head with `ROOT=$PWD bash pkg-available-semantics.sh`.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# What omarchy-pkg-available answers versus what `pacman -S` (omarchy-pkg-add)
# resolves, using the real pacman against a throwaway sync database.
# Run from an omarchy checkout: ROOT=$PWD.
set -uo pipefail
ROOT=${ROOT:-$PWD}
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

mkdir -p "$tmp/db/local" "$tmp/db/sync" "$tmp/gnupg" "$tmp/bin" "$tmp/repo"
echo 9 >"$tmp/db/local/ALPM_DB_VERSION"
entry() { # name provides group
  mkdir -p "$tmp/repo/$1-1.0-1"
  {
    printf '%%FILENAME%%\n%s-1.0-1-any.pkg.tar.zst\n\n%%NAME%%\n%s\n\n%%VERSION%%\n1.0-1\n\n%%ARCH%%\nany\n\n' "$1" "$1"
    [[ -n $2 ]] && printf '%%PROVIDES%%\n%s\n\n' "$2"
    [[ -n $3 ]] && printf '%%GROUPS%%\n%s\n\n' "$3"
  } >"$tmp/repo/$1-1.0-1/desc"
}
entry alacritty "" ""
entry gvim "vim=9.2" ""
entry ttf-a "" fontgroup
(cd "$tmp/repo" && tar -czf "$tmp/db/sync/extra.db" *)
printf '[options]\nDBPath = %s/db/\nGPGDir = %s/gnupg\nSigLevel = Never\n[extra]\nServer = file:///nonexistent\n' "$tmp" "$tmp" >"$tmp/pacman.conf"
printf '#!/bin/bash\nexec /usr/bin/pacman --config %s/pacman.conf "$@"\n' "$tmp" >"$tmp/bin/pacman"
chmod +x "$tmp/bin/pacman"
export PATH="$tmp/bin:$ROOT/bin:$PATH"

printf '%-14s %-22s %s\n' target omarchy-pkg-available "pacman -S resolves to"
for target in alacritty vim fontgroup 'alacritty>=1' --help; do
  omarchy-pkg-available "$target" >/dev/null 2>&1 && avail=true || avail=false
  if [[ $target == -* ]]; then
    resolved="(not a package)"
  else
    resolved=$(pacman -Sp -dd --print-format '%n' -- "$target" 2>&1 | tr '\n' ' ')
  fi
  printf '%-14s %-22s %s\n' "$target" "$avail" "$resolved"
done
```
